subject: humanities
passage: The tappa is the shortest form of Pashto folk poetry, spoken across much of Pakistan and Afghanistan: two lines, the first shorter than the second, sung or recited at gatherings. Tappas are anonymous and have been passed down by word of mouth for generations. A large share of them speak in a woman's voice, about longing for an absent husband, the labor of the household, or a daughter's reluctance to leave her village. The written Pashto literature of the same centuries, by contrast, was produced almost entirely by men. These facts suggest that the tappa ______
stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: was composed mainly by the same poets who wrote the formal literature.
choices.B: has been recorded in writing more carefully than longer forms of Pashto poetry.
choices.C: preserves perspectives that the written literature of the time largely leaves out.
choices.D: was originally sung only by women and later taken up by men.

explanation.why: Written Pashto literature came almost entirely from men, while a large share of anonymous tappas speak with a woman's voice about women's lives. So the oral tappa carries viewpoints that the written record of the period mostly lacks.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The text contrasts anonymous oral tappas with the written literature of men; nothing links the two sets of authors.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Tappas were passed down by word of mouth, so nothing suggests careful written recording.
explanation.C: Correct. Women's voices common in tappas but nearly absent from male-authored written literature make the tappa a record of what the written works omit.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text says many tappas speak in a woman's voice, not that only women sang them or that men took them up later.
